recipes.name: Caramel-Apple Crisp
ingredients_raw: 6 large baking apples, peeled and cut into 1/2-inch slices
0.5 cup cold butter, cut into small pieces

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).
Combine caramel topping and cinnamon in a bowl; stir in apples until evenly coated. Transfer to an 8-inch square baking dish.
Combine flour and brown sugar in the same bowl; cut in butter with a knife or pastry blender until mixture resembles coarse crumbs. Stir in oats; crumble over apples.
Bake in the preheated oven until apples are tender and topping is golden brown, 45 to 50 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Caramel-Apple Crisp
raw_recipe.description: This caramel-apple crisp recipe uses caramel topping, cinnamon, apples, brown sugar, butter, and oats. Serve it with whipped cream or vanilla ice cream.

review.reviewBody: Original review April '11: Great quick dessert. Mine took a little longer because I made my own caramel sauce but other than that, I followed the recipe exact. I like to use Granny Smith's in my crisps, I had nine smallish ones that were just enough for this crisp. I did add a little cinnamon and nutmeg to the topping at the last minute. I have a Kitchen Aid that I used for the topping, I just threw the dry ingredients in the mixer bowl, then my cubed cold butter and let my wisk attachment "cut" my butter into the dry ingredients. Absolutely divine, used on hand ingredients, was cheap to make and VERY soul-soothing to make/eat. I highly recommend you try making your own caramel sauce.......it really takes your dessert over the top. Edited 10/11: I've gotten several e-mails on how to make homemade caramel sauce. This is how I do mine. Mix a quarter cup of butter, one cup of brown sugar, half cup heavy cream OR evaporated milk (depending on what you have on hand), and a pinch of salt in a saucepan over medium low heat. Cook until thick, about seven minutes. You can usually tell, it looks caramel-y. Add a tablespoon of vanilla and cook another minute longer to thicken just a touch more. Pour into a bowl and let it cool a bit before using.

So easy it should be criminal! Like another reviewer, I made my own caramel sauce, which was also super easy (see below). I bumped the cinnamon to 1t, added a touch of allspice and nutmeg, and 1t vanilla to the apple & caramel mixture. I didn't have quick cooking oats so I just used old-fashioned rolled oats, and they gave a nice texture to the topping. This will be my go-to apple crisp recipe. Thanks so much for sharing!
For the caramel sauce:
Melt 1/2C butter (1 stick) over medium heat, whisk in 1C brown sugar, then whisk in 1/4C milk. When smooth, bring to boil then remove from heat. Yeah, that's all there is to it! :)

I only took a microscopic taste of this myself but I could tell from looking over the recipe it was going to be good - and it was, so says Hubs, who was in 7th Heaven eating it. Other than adding the cinnamon to the topping ingredients rather than stirring it into the caramel sauce, I prepared the recipe as written and was quite happy with it just as it stands. I did, however, scale this down to two servings (two beautiful Granny Smith apples from hotel lobby) and baked it in a couple of smallish ramekin type baking dishes (350 degrees, about 35 minutes). This stuff is awesome good - just the right sweetness, crunch and delicate cinnamon flavor. After all, this is CARAMEL apple crisp, so the caramel taste should prevail. I can find absolutely nothing to criticize about this recipe, nor recommend any changes. Neither can Hubs.

Delicious. Used very tart Granny Smith apples which balanced out the sweetness of the other ingredients. A crowd pleaser. Made one with walnuts added to the topping. Very good addition. Also added a touch of nutmeg. I increased the recipe and made a 9 x 13. I let them cook for over an hour to sufficiently soften up the apples.

This is my go to for an apple crisp dessert. I’ve made this several times. The first time as the recipe specifies and then a few times with some slight modifications. I increased the cinnamon mixed with the apples and also added some to the flour and oats. As well, I added crushed pecans to the topping for some extra flavour and texture. Delicious

This is a great and simple recipe! My husband loved it and on my first try he said I should make this for thanksgiving! Definitely a winner, thanks for a great recipe. I used Granny Smith apples and sliced them thin in order to bake faster. I also used salted butter because I felt that I didn't want it to be too sweet. I also doubled up on the crisp topping.

The first time I made this I was impressed with how easy it was but disappointed because it was so watery. The second time around a mixed in two tablespoons of flour with the apple muxture and it came out great. Thanks for the wonderful recipe.

I made this for our Bible Study small group. I doubled the recipe which I thought might be too much but there was only about one serving left. I used Honey Crisp Apples so no sugar needed. Everyone said they loved it. I warmed it before serving and added a scoop of Vanilla/Caramel Ice cream. Yummy
Super easy. I added three times the cinnamon and 3/4 of a jar of caramel sauce. It is amazing!!!

I love the addition of the caramel syrup especially if your apples are a bit on the tart side. Also liked using the apple bowl to mix the topping which picked up any residual caramel and cinnamon. The apples are almost creamy which is what we like. I made a big crisp and then three smaller ones for the freezer. Great recipe! Thanks.
This was a super easy dessert to make! I used Granny Smith apples so it didn’t get too sweet. Love a big scoop with vanilla ice cream and extra caramel sauce!
Great recipe. I will definitely make it again.
I added a cup of crushed walnuts to the mixture. Excellent idea! Easy Peasy and delicious.
The BEST Apple Crisp EVER!! I added some pecan bits to the topping mixture, heavenly!!
Excellent recipe, easy to follow and easy to make...love the extra ingredients of Caramel!
I will definitely make this again. My family scores my cooking and I received five stars for this!
OMG so good
easy delicious and always a fan favorite

What a GREAT recipe! :) I love the Carmel flavor, it makes it so much better I think! I added some more carmel & it tasted better in my opinion. I have never had more compliments on anything that I've baked, I lovvvee this recipe!
